summary:
# NOTES ON THE TWO BOOKS

## BOOK 1 of 2: "Dick Merriwell's Heroic Players; Or, How the Yale Nine Won the Championship" (Burt L. Standish, Street & Smith, copyright 1912; Gutenberg #63608)

**Front matter:** Ad lists of Merriwell series (Nos. 101–221), Alger series, Stratemeyer, Optic, Nick Carter (New Magnet Library, 901–1264), Great Western Library (Diamond Dick / Buffalo Bill by Col. Prentiss Ingraham), Round the World Library (Jack Harkaway). Not story content.

**Main characters:** Jim Phillips (sophomore Yale ace pitcher, captain-elect); Bill Brady (big sophomore catcher, son of wealthy banker, father owns Elm National Bank of New Haven); Harry Maxwell (Jim's ex-roommate); Sam Taylor (senior catcher, former enemy, once a tackle; girlfriend letters); Bob Gray (senior pitcher, Taylor's roommate); Tom Sherman (senior, baseball captain, first base); Steve Carter (third base, once tried to spoil Jim's captaincy; later loyal); Jack Tempest (Virginian sprinter, Jim's friend); Woeful Watson (class pessimist); Dick Merriwell (universal coach, "Y.M.C.A.-style" ideal; boxer); Jackson (second base, quarterback, later football captain); Gurney (sophomore bettor); Carpenter (thin, bespectacled grind, glasses); Shesgren (small, blue eyes, thick glasses, thin reedy voice, sophomore grind); Wesley Parker (junior, big guard, football, drinks; bully); Foote / Paul Foote (undersized, chain-smoking, rich dad, gambling debts); Danby (former football captain); Hasbrook (New Haven Country Club captain, old Yale man); Chetwind (real-estate broker, country-club member, sent $100 registered letter); Bowen (Harvard catcher/captain, Andover friend of Brady); Briggs (Harvard pitcher, control); Wooley (Harvard pitcher); Hobson (famous ex-Harvard pitcher); Reid, Farquar, Renshaw, Hazlitt (Harvard batters); Winston (substitute pitcher, Yale); Harding (gambler, Bill Harding, father dying in asylum, New Haven boss; political power in NY); Barrows (gambler, "Pete," socialist con man); Svenson (Scandinavian skipper of yacht *Marina*, drunk); Dennison (weak gambler, backer); Bascom (wireless man, ex-liner operator); Marsten ("Johnny," gambler, owns house with code bell, Elm St.); Riggs (paying teller, Elm National, stole $1000); Hazen (stout gambler, bribed Merriwell, bought umpire Derring); Wescott (man in blue); Derring (umpire, crooked; in Book 1 Ch. (Merry's Omaha?) — no, Derring is in Book 2); Hank Dowling/Bates (Book 2); Neilson (Harvard crew coach); Benton & Hargreaves (Yale assistant crew coaches); Murchison (crew captain/stroke); Flagg (No. 7); Rogers (coxswain); Thompson (Harvard coach); Canfield (professor, history exam); Sam (old Black rubber, "Marse Dick"); Detective Jones (New Haven police); Bromlow (bank president, Elm National); Hastings (cashier); Phelps (high financier, Maine lumber rival); Arlington (Chester, engineer; sister June, Dick's love interest); Gifford Pinchot mentioned; Felicia is in Book 2 only.

**Plot, in order:**
1. Jim, Bill, Harry discuss Harvard (Briggs pitched shutouts vs Cornell, Penn, Amherst; Bowen catches him). Practice at field; Dick praises "inside baseball."
2. Gurney bets; Watson pessimism; Carpenter/Shesgren resent Jim; Parker overhears, recruits them to frame Jim. Parker wants Carter as captain; Tempest insults-exchange with Parker.
3. Jim invited by Hasbrook to pitch for New Haven Country Club vs Boston Athletic Association; Dick consents on conditions (Brady to watch arm). Chetwind secretly sends $100 registered letter; Parker's trap via Shesgren as go-between. Parker drunk on porch.
4. Game in New Haven (Wed): Jim v Hobson; Bowen; Brady homers; Hasbrook wins 10th-ish in 9th (tied 6-6 after 6; New Haven wins on Hasbrook drop + wild throw). Jim has "second registered letter" missing; Carpenter visits Jim.
5. Dick reviews Boston infield tricks. Bowen (Harvard captain) files protest: Jim professional, $100 registered letter, receipt signed by Jim. Chetwind confirms, won't name agent.
6. Dick investigates; Chetwind's office; Jim denies; letter missing; Brady recalls Carpenter visited. Carter tells Dick Parker blurted charge at football meeting. Carter suspects conspiracy.
7. Parker's football captaincy: meeting postponed by Taylor/Sherman motion (Danby recalled). Parker threatens Merriwell.
8. Parker confronts Shesgren; ties him up with trunk strap; takes letter, money marked (Chetwind's bill numbers); plants letter in Jim's room. Carpenter sent to see Jim.
9. Brady/Jim find slit envelope with a folded blank sheet; post-office inspector visits; Chetwind names Shesgren as agent.
10. Shesgren freed, confesses. Dick breaks Parker's alibi by matching knife nick; Parker confesses, withdraws candidacy. Jim forgives Carpenter.
11. Harvard protest withdrawn; team goes to Boston (Hotel in Back Bay). Jim kidnapped from taxi by Parker's men near Boston; taken to seaside. Jim steals/flies biplane from Squantum, lands at Harvard field; arrives in time. Game 1 at Cambridge: Yale wins 1–0; Jim's wild pitch trick with cap; Brady runs back.
12. Foote & Parker plot against Gray & Taylor (planted cribbing notes). Gray forbidden; Winston pitches; Harvard wins game 2 by one run; Gray returns in 9th, strikes out three.
13. Dick finds finger-prints on crib (Foote's bread-print later), Jim lured into freight car by Foote's ventriloquism (Parker tells Dick); Foote caught via bread; Jim rescued from car No. 34576 (Big Four) at Kingston NY. Jim pitches Game 3 at Polo Grounds, lefthanded triple play; Yale wins championship 3–2. Jim elected captain.
14. Crew trouble: freshmen beat varsity; betting syndicate Svenson/Barrows/Dennison, *Marina* plot with magnet in shell keels. Jim hides aboard *Marina*, sinks it; Dick and Neilson investigate. Swapped shells. Race: Yale wins 4-mile race by under 2 seconds; Barrows' miniature clockwork torpedo foiled by Jim in hydroplane.
15. Boston wants revenge: second Country Club game set for July 4 (Briggs v Jim).
16. Barrows (Pete) and Bascom plot bank robbery of Elm National; Foote used; Riggs; watchman shot with slingshot; Jim discovered in vault; counterfeit $5000 deposit traced; Barrows arrested in NY, sentenced 5 yrs; Riggs suspended sentence.
17. Final game (July 4, New Haven): Jim pitches; Boston wins early (7–4); Jim recovers; wins 8–7 in 9th with bunt/Brady single/Carter double. Final line "THE END" with next title No. 212 "Dick Merriwell at the Olympics" / No. 76 "Dick Merriwell at Fardale."

Key quotes: "Inside baseball"; Dick: "It isn't on the field that baseball championships are won." Jim's hydroplane; "Wait!" (Dick).

---

## BOOK 2 of 2: "Frank Merriwell's Support; Or, A Triple Play" (Burt L. Standish, Street & Smith, copyright 1901; Gutenberg #62719)

**Main characters:** Frank Merriwell (Yale graduate, pitcher, wrist sprained, uses "double-shoot" reverse curve); Dick Merriwell (younger brother, ~14, boy wonder, pitches with both hands, "jump ball"; raised in West, Pleasant Valley, Lake Sunshine, Rockies); Old Joe Crowfoot (Indian, dirty red blanket, black pipe; once shot; ally of Dick; says "Heap," "Injun Heart," "Steady Hand" = Frank); Felicia (Dick's love, "Little Star Eyes," daughter of Mr. Delores); Juan Delores (Spanish refugee, Dick's early guardian); Bart Hodge (catcher); Jack Ready (third base, witty, Shakespearean speech); Harry Rattleton (second base, "dim-jandy" malapropisms); Berlin Carson (rf/ss); Bruce Browning (1st base, big, lazy); Joe Gamp (cf, long-legged New Hampshire youth, stutters); John Swiftwing (lf, Indian, ex-Carlisle); Greg Carker (socialist-talk, bunt/ss); Omaha Stars: Dorrity (captain, 1st base), Batch (pitcher), Hanson (catcher, heavy hitter), Jack (2d b), Maloney (rf, red-headed), Corrigan (3d b), Teller, Skew, O'Grady, Ready... Derring (crooked umpire), Hazen (stout gambler, red face, "Hazen," bribes), Wescott (man in blue, bets $200), Chop Morrisy (replacement umpire), Wilson (manager of Stars), Livingstone; Hank Dowling (gambler, dark, hunched), Charley Bates (pale, inherited million, opium fiend), Pete (cross-eyed waiter, poisons vichy). Minneapolis: Stebson, Trueman (St. Paul captain), Foley, Prince, Keen, Webber, Foley's injury, jay pitcher (disguised Frank, "Bill"; stammering friend Joe). Philadelphia: Nick Robinson (manager), Jack Wilder, Bud McCann (prizefighter-catcher), Jim "Squinty" McCann (bully), Bowers, Nesbitt, Waldron, Hayward, Flobert, Joiler, Maloney, Webster, McGlinkey. New York: Jack Hazard (white-haired, challenges via "The Mysteries," Yale team of old college friends: Gene Skelding (3b, reformed), Starbright (1b), Mason (ss), Oliver Packard (2b), Dismal Jones (lf), Hans Dunnerwurst (rf), Barney Mulloy (c, Irish), Ephraim Gallup (cf, farm boy), Dade Morgan (pitcher, sweet smile). Inza Burrage and Elsie Bellwood (girls with Yale flags; Elsie loves Bart). Man with a huge St. Bernard, Nero (the dog).

**Plot, in order:**
1. Ch. I–IV: 7th inning, Omaha Stars; Frank's wrist sprained; Hanson homer; Gamp throws to plate; Bart tags Hanson; Frank pitches on despite pain. Frank wins by 3-2 later? Actually Stars win game 1 by 3-2 after umpire Derring's bad calls, Stars' Corrigan wins in 9th; Frank refuses to yield, Derring mobbed; Frank protects him, ejects him.
2. Ch. V: Team lament; Frank challenges Stars for next day (winner takes gate); overhears Wilson; Derring insults; Frank punches Derring; Hazen's revolver disarmed by Frank.
3. Ch. VI–VII: Dick arrives with Crowfoot; Frank asks Joe to stay; Dick bets Hazen $1000 (Frank forbids betting; Dick's money given to charity); Game 2: Dick pitches; Dick catches/steals; Merriwell wins 1-0? Score 1–1 then Dick wins in 9th; Hazen loses.
4. Ch. VIII–IX: Dick's brilliant game (catches, stolen bases, 1–1 tie, then winning run in 9th, Bart's hit).
5. Ch. X–XV: Minneapolis/St. Paul. Foley spiked by Prince; jay pitcher (disguised Frank) takes mound, double-shoot ("in and out"), tying home run; Old Joe's war-whoop; Dowling tries to bribe; fight; Yale cheers; song "Here's to good old Merry"; Frank challenged to rematch. Frank reveals identity.
6. Ch. XVI–XIX: Vichy water drugged by Pete (Dowling's plan); Frank dizzy; Dick pitches; Old Joe war-dance; Frank home run over right-field fence wins 2-1 (Merriwell ninth-inning home run).
7. Ch. XIX–XXI: Philadelphia; Dick fights Squinty Jim (who tried to attack Old Joe with urchins); policeman's son reformed by Frank; Frank's challenge to Athletics; Bud McCann bat-trip; McCann spikes; triple play by Dick unassisted (Dick tags Robinson); win 5–4.
8. Ch. XXVI–XXVIII: Jack Hazard challenges Frank to Polo Grounds vs "The Mysteries"; Dick homesick (Felicia); Old Joe's advice. Dick pitches; Old Joe kills mad dog (Nero) with knife; owner blames Joe; Joe searched, knife hidden by Carson; Dick's stolen home wins 6–5? Final score: Merriwell wins in 9th when Dick steals home after Ready's bunt; Inza and Elsie: Inza gives Dick the Yale blue badge; Elsie kisses Dick.

**Ending:** "THE END." Next: No. 76 "Dick Merriwell at Fardale," Burt L. Standish.

Transcriber's notes list corrected misprints (e.g., p.110 "went over third," p.222 "Bud McCann," p.315 "Gamp was earnest").
